result.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
result.summary: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

AI.brief_summary: 提出 loom attention：让每个 token 的注意力在「垂直」方向（对先前 head 输出计算 query/key/value）与「水平」方向（对 token）交织，从而动态重连电路；用归一化门控线性注意力在 per-token 矩阵记忆上实例化，形成把控制与内容分配到向量流和矩阵流的双流 LoomFormer。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「垂直注意力 + 矩阵记忆充当第二残差流」提供了跨层 latent 状态如何被后续层压缩、取用与更新的具体机制线索，可供核查 LVR 中视觉信息在内部状态里的保留与坍缩问题；但论文仅在语言建模上验证，与视觉证据筛选的联系尚属推测。
